tasks.focus: Map the architecture, trust boundaries, user roles, entry points, security controls and existing tests. Read executable code rather than relying on documentation. Identify the highest-risk surfaces for follow-up review.

Review authentication, authorization, session handling, role transitions, tenant isolation and account recovery. Trace concrete request paths and distinguish source observations from tests that were not executed.
Review backend and API behavior, validation, ownership checks, error handling, concurrency boundaries and external integrations. Identify concrete runtime scenarios needed to verify suspected issues.
Review web and mobile clients, navigation guards, state handling, empty and error states, accessibility-sensitive paths and client/server contract mismatches. Do not claim a live UI test ran.
Review data classification, logging, retention, deletion, consent, export, secret handling and third-party data flows. Flag claims that require legal or runtime confirmation.

Cross-check every handoff against source, reconcile contradictions, rank suspected issues by evidence and impact, and produce a concrete isolated test plan. Keep source observations, suspected issues and unexecuted tests clearly separated.
